propositions: A configured provider is silently dropped when the model id contains a colon, because _resolve_target tests for colon presence rather than provider-qualifier syntax, misinterpreting version suffixes as qualifiers.
Canonical Bedrock model ids in the form 'anthropic.claude-*-v1:0' fail resolution with a misleading error message naming a fragment of the model id instead of the actual provider.
Two independent colon-scan implementations (_resolve_target and infer_provider) diverge in their interpretation, causing the same bug to manifest through different code paths.
An explicitly configured provider must be checked before scanning the model string, so that punctuation in model ids cannot overrule explicit configuration.
An already-qualified model string must not be double-prefixed, preserving backward compatibility with inline-qualified forms.
Conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pairs must raise rather than silently picking a winner, preventing loss of explicit instruction.
